touches.text: build_inspector: python sieves run after a build; reds a component that fails one (no charter, no proofs, a silent device, ...). "We find a new thing, we add a new sieve." → CodeMother (10.3.5)

ROOT INTENTION for checks and gates (Akien, 2026-10-27): the inspector does all the checks, so there is no need for more checks anywhere else. The inspector's output is consumed by the gate. The gate's output is the certificate. "This was how I meant it all along."
Entry gates exist only to kick back what doesn't meet the entry requirements. Nothing in them is about who writes what.

Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve. (Not diagnostic_inspector: it is base's, 17.3.) The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)
